Revolutionary farm tech turns science fiction into reality

Slideshow: Staff share their favorite products from this year’s Farm Progress Show, from solar-powered tractors to autonomous scouting robots.

Andy Castillo,Editor of Farm Equipment and Machinery,Farm ProgressSeptember 19, 2026

photo_library6 Slides

play_arrowStart slideshow

Another Farm Progress Show might have come to an end, but the technological advancements showcased there are moving faster than ever. Today’s agricultural technology is reaching heights perceived as unachievable a decade ago; the cutting edge is quickly becoming commonplace. Drones fly above corn crops, while robots operate tractors.

A slew of new products was launched into the marketplace during this year’s show Sept. 1-3. Fendt brought two new tractors and an 80-foot momentum planter to market, while John Deere announced its AI assistant, JD. Case IH and New Holland announced updates to their forage harvester lineups, and Claas unveiled three new tractor lines.

It’s an exciting time for agriculture technology, and Farm Progress editors have a front-row seat to watch its evolution. Here’s what caught their interest this year.

About the Author

Andy Castillo

Editor of Farm Equipment and Machinery, Farm Progress

Andy Castillo started his career in journalism about a decade ago as a television news cameraperson and producer before transitioning to a regional newspaper covering western Massachusetts, where he wrote about local farming. Between military deployments with the Air Force and covering the news, he earned an MFA in creative nonfiction writing from Bay Path University, building on the English degree he earned from the University of Massachusetts Amherst. In his role at Farm Progress, Castillo covers agricultural technology, new machinery and the constantly evolving farm equipment marketplace.

Castillo splits his time between the open road and western Massachusetts with his wife, Brianna, a travel nurse who specializes in pediatric oncology, and their rescue pup, Rio. When not attending farm shows, Castillo enjoys playing music, snowboarding, writing, cooking and restoring their 1920 craftsman bungalow. You can find Castillo at farm machinery shows across the country.

在今年的展会（9月1日至3日）期间，大量新产品投放市场。Fendt推出了两款新拖拉机和一台80英尺的Momentum播种机，而John Deere发布了其AI助手JD。Case IH和New Holland宣布了其饲草收获机产品线的更新，Claas则推出了三条新拖拉机产品线。

对于农业技术而言，这是一个激动人心的时代，Farm Progress的编辑们拥有前排座位来观察其演变。以下是今年引起他们兴趣的内容。
